=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: "Telegram review-blocked judge decision" step, the `merge)` arm (lines 6759-6761): `MSG="Review-blocked judge merged PR as-is"` with `JUDGE_ALERT_LEVEL="DEBUG"`
  Problem: `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` writes `judge_handled=true` and `judge_action=merge` unconditionally at lines 2095-2096 and 2151-2152, after a merge it may not have requested or that did not land.
  Why it fails at runtime: The workflow still sends "Review-blocked judge merged PR as-is", which is false in these cases. The message is now DEBUG, so the default `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=WARNING` drops it. Before this change it paged at CRITICAL. A rejected `gh pr merge` (branch protection, permissions) or a failed checks wait therefore produces no page and a false log message, until the stall ladder eventually escalates.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: `_standalone_conflict_count_attempt`, lines 26438-26443 (`reason=marker_outside_window`), together with `_STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STATE_LOADED="partial"` set at 26558
  Problem: When the PR has more than 100 comments (`hasPreviousPage` is true) and the last 100 contain no marker by the pipeline's own login, the function logs `outcome=skip reason=marker_outside_window` and returns. It does not count the attempt and does not write a marker.
  Why it fails at runtime: The marker is edited in place with PATCH, so it keeps its old position in the comment list. Once newer comments push it past the last 100, every later attempt on that PR takes this branch. The count never reaches `STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STUCK_ALERT_ATTEMPTS`, and the stuck-conflict WARNING can never fire.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description, "Review / autofix: Moved to DEBUG: … the judge's stall-recovery-retry skips and its `merge_conflict` skip", and the convention that DEBUG means the pipeline already owns the event.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, the skip-reason `case` in "Telegram review-blocked judge decision" (lines 6777-6814), with a `base_moved_overlap)` arm.
  Evidence of absence: `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` line 2617 emits `judge_skip_reason=base_moved_overlap` after `_pr_base_fresh_for_merge` has requested a branch update ("branch update requested; merge_with_followup deferred"). The `synchronize` run then re-validates the PR on its own. This is the same kind of retry the pipeline owns as `blocking_check_runs`, which already has a DEBUG arm. The `case` has no `base_moved_overlap)` arm, so the reason falls to `*)` (lines 6812-6813). That arm keeps CRITICAL and says "autofix exhausted … Needs human intervention", which is false here. A person is paged for a self-clearing deferral, which is the behaviour this PR sets out to remove.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6759-6761 (`merge)` arm in "Telegram review-blocked judge decision" step)
  Problem: The `merge)` arm sends "Review-blocked judge merged PR as-is" at `JUDGE_ALERT_LEVEL="DEBUG"`, but `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` emits `judge_action=merge` in many paths where no merge actually happened.
  Why it fails at runtime: In each failure path, the Telegram message and the DEBUG level falsely claim the action succeeded. A person who sees only Telegram learns that the PR merged or was reissued, so they stop looking at it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 26438-26443 (`_standalone_conflict_count_attempt`, inside the `if [ "${found}" != "true" ] && [ "${loaded}" = "partial" ]` block)
  Problem: when `loaded="partial"` and `found="false"`, the function returns early with `reason=marker_outside_window` and never writes a new marker and never increments the counter.
  Why it fails at runtime: A standalone PR with 100+ comments and a conflict keeps the conflict-attempt counter at 0 forever; the per-head WARNING never fires.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6765-6767 (`close_and_reissue)` arm)
  Problem: `review_rb_judge.sh` emits `judge_action=close_and_reissue` even when the replacement issue was not created.
  Why it fails at runtime: The original PR is closed and the human is paged with the false claim that a replacement issue was created. There is no follow-up tracking the work.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description operator decision Q1/A1 — "demote auto-handled alerts to DEBUG and default `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` to WARNING". The same auto-handled principle applies to `judge_skip_reason=base_moved_overlap`: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh line 2617 emits it after "branch update requested; merge_with_followup deferred", and the synchronize run re-validates automatically.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, the `JUDGE_SKIP_REASON` `case` statement in "Telegram review-blocked judge decision" (lines 6777-6814), adding a `base_moved_overlap)` arm.
  Evidence of absence: no `base_moved_overlap)` arm in the `case` at lines 6777-6814; the reason falls through to `*)` at lines 6812-6813, which keeps `JUDGE_ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"` and prints "PR review blocked — autofix exhausted (N iterations)\nNeeds human intervention". For `base_moved_overlap` no human is needed; the synchronize run handles it. The shipped test `test_review_blocked_judge_successes_are_debug` only covers the `JUDGE_HANDLED=true` arms and does not cover the `JUDGE_HANDLED=false` skip-reason `case`, so this regression is unguarded.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description operator decision Q3/A3 — "the standalone conflict sweep now counts resolution attempts per PR head and sends one `WARNING` after `STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STUCK_ALERT_ATTEMPTS` attempts".
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, the `_standalone_conflict_count_attempt` function around lines 26438-26443.
  Evidence of absence: the `if [ "${found}" != "true" ] && [ "${loaded}" = "partial" ]` block at lines 26438-26443 returns early without writing a marker, so PRs whose 100-comment window has scrolled past the last PATCHed marker never see the counter advance past 0; the `WARNING` documented in the requirement never fires. The test `test_conflict_truncated_window_without_trusted_marker_skips` codifies the broken behaviour.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
